strategies.name: Direct Network Flood Detection across IaaS, Linux, Windows, and macOS

analytics.name: Analytic 0969
analytics.guidance: High-volume packet generation by local processes (e.g., PowerShell, cmd, curl.exe) or network service processes resulting in excessive outbound traffic over short time window, correlated with abnormal resource usage or degraded host responsiveness.

tuning.description: Defines the burst threshold (e.g., 10,000 pps) above which activity should be flagged as anomalous.
Duration over which to aggregate and analyze flow volume.

analytics.name: Analytic 0970
analytics.guidance: Kernel or userland processes generating high-rate network traffic (ICMP, UDP, TCP SYN) beyond expected interface throughput or user behavior norms.

tuning.description: Threshold of repeated socket calls within a short interval indicating flood behavior.
Restrict to non-admin user traffic unless elevated access is detected.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: connect or sendto system call with burst pattern

analytics.name: Analytic 0971
analytics.guidance: Excessive outbound traffic via `ping`, `curl`, or custom scripts indicating flooding behavior, especially with no UI context or user interaction.

tuning.description: Tunable range (e.g., 15s, 30s) for detecting packet floods.

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: process created with repeated ICMP or UDP flood behavior

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: sudden burst in outgoing packets from same PID

analytics.name: Analytic 0972
analytics.guidance: VM or cloud instance generating anomalously high network egress targeting same destination IP or service, especially using stateless protocols.

tuning.description: Alert when egress exceeds normal usage by X%.
Prioritize alerts on stateless protocols such as UDP and ICMP.

log_sources.name: AWS:VPCFlowLogs
log_sources.channel: source instance sends large volume of traffic in short window
